what_happened: Job 20261031-150034-17c3 (push candidates to athena/ci/<job id> and use GitHub's result in checks) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic judged the design sound. One major finding remained. The planned tests for criteria 1–3 set origin to a github.com https URL. That makes check_and_verify call early_pr (run/mod.rs:1201), which outside early_seam uses the real GhCli and a real git push. The plan never installs early_seam, so its main demonstrations would make real network calls, which the request forbids, and could hang or flake. Two minor findings: the ci.yml trigger comment would be wrong after only on.push.branches changes, and a resumed job with checks recorded earlier from CI gives the verifier no reuse statement. One nit: the fake runs reply should exercise the aggregate-job verdict. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that the seams a plan names exist and that its demonstrations go through the real entry point. It does not require the plan to trace every side-effecting call on that path for the fixture it chose, such as the origin value, and show each is faked or skipped. Here a github.com origin silently enables early_pr, which is a sibling writer of the very pull-request and push behavior being changed. The code has two fake seams (gh::Runner and early_seam), and the plan covered only one. Planning has three fixed rounds and keeps no partial plan, so a major finding in round 3 loses all planning spend. Nothing offers a cheap repair step for a gap that reading the code would settle. This is the same job line as the earlier CI-source case 20261031-142728-4hsq, whose fix produced this plan, so each round exposes another path in the same flow.
prevention: Add a planning check, run before the critic rounds end, that lists every external-effect call (network, gh, git push, process spawn) reachable from each demonstration's entry point under the fixture's config. It requires the plan to name the fake or skip for each one, or to state that the fixture avoids it. A test harness guard would also make any unfaked real network or gh call in a test fail immediately. Also let a final round that has only one mechanical major finding get one targeted repair pass that keeps the plan, instead of failing the job.
proposed_request: Retry job 20261031-150034-17c3: push each candidate to athena/ci/<job id> and use GitHub's CI result for that exact pushed SHA in the job's checks. Keep the plan's accepted design: `with_ci_source` chooses the source and the wait together so a no-remote job does not wait over NoCi; use only the push run on athena/ci/<job id>; force-push to clear a branch left by a killed job; delete the branch once, in `dispatch`; judge by the aggregate job. Fix the gaps the critic found. (1) Tests for the CI criteria must make no real network, gh or git push call. If a test origin is a github.com URL, install `early_seam` in that test (or use an origin that does not trigger `early_pr`), and add a test that fails if any real gh or push is attempted. (2) Update the trigger comment in .github/workflows/ci.yml together with `on.push.branches`. (3) When a resumed job reuses checks recorded earlier from CI, give the verifier a statement saying so. (4) Make the fake runs reply exercise the aggregate-job verdict in both the green and red tests. Allowed files: the code and test files the plan touches in crates/athena-core (run/mod.rs, run/ci.rs, run/ci_tests.rs, run/tests.rs, run/verification.rs, gh/early.rs, gh/tests.rs, gh/client.rs), .github/workflows/ci.yml, and the changelog.
